blocks.h2: Signs Your Sump Pump Needs Attention
blocks.intro: Don't wait for the next storm:

tiles.body: Pour water in the pit. No start means a float or motor problem.
A stuck float, a failed check valve or a pump that's too small.
Worn bearings or debris in the impeller.
A storm that knocks out power leaves you unprotected.

blocks.intro: In September 2008, about 9 inches of rain fell on Geneva in two days, and basements flooded across much of Kane County.

items.body: Many historic homes had sump pits added long after they were built. Some are small or shallow and struggle in a big storm.
More than 4 in 10 homes were built after 1990. Many still have their original builder-grade pumps, and those are past their prime.
Storms knock out power. A backup keeps pumping when the main pump can't.
A short or frozen discharge line sends water right back to the foundation.

blocks.h2: Sump Pump Questions From Geneva Homeowners

items.q: Can you install a sump pump in an old basement without one?
items.answer: Often, yes. We cut a pit in the floor, connect any drain tile and run a discharge line outside. We'll assess the foundation first.

items.q: How long do sump pumps last?
items.answer: Most last somewhere around 7 to 10 years, less if they run often.

items.q: Do I need a battery backup?
items.preview: If you have a finished basement, yes.
items.answer: If your basement is finished or holds anything you care about, yes.
Outside, onto the yard or into a storm line, far enough from the house that it doesn't soak back in. Never into the sanitary sewer.

items.q: How much does sump pump installation cost in Geneva?
items.preview: It depends on the pump, pit and backup. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the pump, any pit or check valve work and whether you add a backup. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
